text:
Lawson Crouse is doing the Lawson Crouse things. He has 59 hits, his ice time is up about two minutes over his last ten games, and at five on five the Mammoth take 58% of the expected goals when he's on the ice. What's missing is the scoring: 2 goals on 5.4 expected, a 5% shooting percentage for a player who usually sits somewhere between 11% and 16%.

That's a big gap for a power forward who scored 24 last season, and it's almost all finishing. His chance quality is about where it was a year ago. Evolving-Hockey had him 110th among forwards last season, with most of his value from even-strength offense, so the goals have a track record behind them.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows a side of his game people miss: 18% of his setups go across the royal road, the side-to-side pass that moves a goalie, more than double a typical forward. Twenty-three games of 5% shooting from a player like this reads as bad luck. Watch the shot count; the goals should follow it.
headline: Lawson Crouse is hitting everything but the net
